text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Krupp KFHG.F abandons hostile takeover bid for rival Thyssen.
- Talks between government and opposition on energy policy, including the storage of nuclear waste, fail to produce an agreement.
- Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel praises European integration on 40th anniversary of signing of Treaties of Rome.
- Construction firm Hochtief AG to announce plans which would give it indirect conrol of rival Philipp Holzmann AG by pooling Hochtief and Deutsche Bank shares in the company.
HANDELSBLATT
- Media group Kirch to get big credit line from private and public banks.
- Kinkel rejects need for referendum on planned single European currency.
- Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) and German Trade Union Confederation (DGB) warn against cutting social spending to meet criteria for single currency.
- Liberalisation of air traffic rules between European Union countries from April 1 will bring few cheap flights initially.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Federal Insurance Office approves applications by health insurance funds to raise contributions.
- German government dissatisfied with European Commission proposals for "stability pact" for planned single currency.
- Deutsche Bank board member Ulrich Cartellieri says he considering resigning from Thyssen supervisory board.
DIE WELT
- Positions of government and opposition harden over tax policy. Impression grows that talks between them will fail.
- Thyssen workers protest against role of Deutsche Bank in Krupp's takeover bid.
- Federal Court of Justice says bank customers can claim compensation if badly advised by banks about investments.
